info.album: Peggy Sue (Live On The Ed Sullivan Show, December 1, 1957)

podcast.body: This song, originally titled "Cindy Lu" after Holly's niece, was re-recorded on July 2, 1957, with lyrics changed to honor Jerry Allison's girlfriend, Peggy Sue Garrison. Its unique sound involved Allison playing a fast paviddle on snare drums outside the main studio and producer Norman Petty using an echo chamber with a flicking switch, making it sound like two drummers. Buddy Holly also had Nikki Sullivan flick a pickup switch on his guitar during the fast solo for tonal changes. It eventually reached number three on the charts. "Peggy Sue hid number three."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 74: "It Doesn't Matter Any More" by Buddy Holly

podcast.body: Tommy Steele inaccurately claimed to have seen Buddy Holly perform this song in Norfolk, Virginia, in 1955, sparking his interest in rock and roll. However, Holly didn't meet Peggy Sue Gehrman (the song's namesake) until 1956, and the song itself wasn't written until 1957. "the song doesn't seem to have been written until 1957."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
